claim_verdicts.evidence: The core point is backed by slo.md's 'Nguồn' column (lines 62-67): every row names a need (shops selling, CH-3, YC-7), none a measured reading. The 'first guess' part is presented in §6 with an explicit condition ("when no need is written down yet, if it is replaced once one is"), so it is a conditioned recommendation, not opinion-as-fact.

Round 2: §4 now uses the suggested_text ("the team should see it while there is room before the contract is broken"), diagram edge "lower, so room before a breach", summary item 4 "can see". Matches slo.md line 77, stated as intent: "SLA thấp hơn SLO có chủ ý: đội thấy vấn đề và sửa trước khi hợp đồng bị vi phạm."

Follows from the numbers in slo.md (S1 SLO 99.5%, line 64): a 99.9% promise is missed at any ratio between 99.5% and 99.9%, a range where the SLO is still met. The advice is conditioned ("only if the team can keep it", "If the need has not changed") as written in §7.

Round 2: §6 row now reads "matches how the SLA in `slo.md` and its credits are counted". slo.md lines 75-76: "99% ... trong mỗi tháng dương lịch. Tháng nào thấp hơn, cửa hàng được bồi hoàn bằng tín dụng dịch vụ trừ vào kỳ sau." Rolling-window part is arithmetic (line 60: 28 ngày trượt).

issues.text: New in round 2: the sentence derives the 100% rule from the policy, but the policy (slo.md lines 92-94) still lets fixes and reliability work ship after a miss; only feature releases stop. 'Fix reliability first' followed by 'a bug-fix release would not be safe' pulls in two directions. slo.md line 71 reaches 'bug-fix releases included' directly: at 100% any change that can cause one failure misses the target.
issues.quote: The team treats a miss as a reason to hold back risky changes and fix reliability first, so at 100% no change that might fail would be safe, a release that fixes a bug included.
issues.fix: Replace with: "The team treats a miss as a reason to hold back risky changes. At 100%, any change that might cause a single failure would miss the target, so even a release that fixes a bug carries that risk."

issues.text: New in round 2, in the changed sentence. issues.quote: The team treats a miss as a reason to hold back risky changes and fix reliability first, so at 100% no change that might fail would be safe, a release that fixes a bug included.
